title: WHO: about 300,000 drowning deaths a year, mostly in poorer countries
summary: WHO's drowning fact sheet gives the scale and the age pattern. It is a count of deaths, not a rescue method.
body: The World Health Organization's drowning fact sheet, opened 2026-11-18, says there are around 300,000 annual drowning deaths worldwide. Children under 5 account for nearly a quarter. Drowning is the fourth leading cause of death for children aged 1 to 4 and the third for children aged 5 to 14. Ninety-two percent of drowning deaths occur in low- and middle-income countries. Since 2000 the global drowning death rate has fallen by 38 percent, from 6.1 to 3.8 per 100,000. Children and young adults aged 0 to 29 account for 57 percent of drowning deaths. The sheet says drowning accounts for 75 percent of deaths in flood disasters. Those are WHO's figures on that page. They are not a procedure for pulling someone out of water.
